title: Veterans Pension One-Time Declarations — Compensation Release Months Before and After the Pension Effective Date
content:
**Principle.** Compensation paid to the veteran counts as income for pension only for months before pension was first paid; compensation paid for a month that pension also paid is settled against the pension for that month and is not counted as income.

**Rule for a Veterans Pension one-time payment declaration.** The releases in the period declared, less the fee taken out, count by the months the most recent retroactive Disability Compensation release was paid for — the first and last months of the period that release covers, as shown in the compensation payment ledger — compared with the pension effective date:

| Months the most recent release was paid for | Share that counts |
|---|---|
| every month came before the pension effective date | in full — a share of 1 |
| first month before the pension effective date, months running into the effective month or later | the months before pension was first paid divided by all the months it was paid for |
| every month is a month of pension | none — settled against the pension |

The months before pension was first paid are the whole months from the release's first month to the pension effective date plus the months by which pension payment starts after its effective date (the product's payment start lag, 1 month). All the months it was paid for are counted from its first month through its last month, both included.

## Worked example (hypothetical)

Pension effective 2025-06-01. Most recent release paid for 2025-01 through 2025-12: 12 months paid for. Whole months from 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-01: 5; plus the 1-month lag: 6. Share: 6 divided by 12. On releases of 10000.00 less no fee, 5000.00 counts before any weighting for the date of deposit.

A release paid for 2024-07 through 2025-04 — every month before the June 2025 effective date — counts in full; one paid for 2025-07 through 2025-09 counts nothing.
